label: Moral-property supervenience with modal strength not yet specified
definition: No moral-property difference without some difference in nonmoral or natural properties. An explicit world domain, property base, individuation and modal quantifier are still needed to determine whether this is a within-world, cross-world local or whole-world global supervenience principle.
note: Railton, Moral Realism, p.165 directly endorses moral-on-natural supervenience while withholding full reduction. Van Roojen, Moral Cognitivism vs. Non-Cognitivism §3.4 distinguishes the property thesis from appropriate predication and the still stronger analytic competence demand. This definition does not select the `Weak` or `Strong` Boolean-profile predicates and has no Lean declaration. OPEN: which properties constitute the total natural base, how things/worlds are matched, modal strength and the justification of the necessity. It neither asserts grounding nor supplies a moral criterion.
